steps.title: Create or sign in to your Harvest account and open Developers (Harvest ID)
steps.detail: Log into Harvest and go to the Developers section at id.getharvest.com/developers to create an OAuth2 Application or generate Personal Access Tokens.

evidence.note: Docs reference the Developers section for creating apps and personal tokens.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: Register a new OAuth2 Application
steps.detail: Provide Name, Redirect URL, whether you support multiple accounts, and select Products (Harvest, Forecast or both). Copy the returned Client ID and Client Secret.

evidence.note: Registration fields and process described in the OAuth docs and demonstrated in the walkthrough video.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: Implement Authorization Code flow (build connect button and redirect)
steps.detail: Generate an authorization URL using https://id.getharvest.com/oauth2/authorize with client_id and response_type=code, include state and redirect_uri, and implement the redirect handler to receive the code.

evidence.note: Authorization endpoint, parameters and redirect behavior described in the docs.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: Exchange authorization code for tokens server-side
steps.detail: POST to https://id.getharvest.com/api/v2/oauth2/token with code, client_id, client_secret and grant_type=authorization_code; store access_token and refresh_token securely.

evidence.note: Token exchange endpoint and example requests/responses are documented.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: Implement refresh token flow and API calls
steps.detail: Use the documented refresh token POST to the same token endpoint to obtain new access tokens before expiry; call Harvest API endpoints with Authorization: Bearer <access_token> and Harvest-Account-Id header where required.

evidence.note: Docs include refresh token example and header usage for API requests.
evidence.label: sourced

steps.title: Test end-to-end in dev and deploy redirect endpoint
steps.detail: Authorize with a test Harvest account, exchange the code, verify token lifetimes and API access, then deploy the redirect callback to your production URL and update the app registration if needed.

evidence.note: Video and docs show end-to-end flow and practical testing steps.
evidence.label: sourced

nuances.text: Access tokens have long expiry in Harvest examples: example response shows expires_in = 1209600 (14 days).

evidence.note: The API example response includes expires_in with value 1209600 seconds.
evidence.label: sourced

nuances.text: Personal Access Tokens exist and are useful for single-user scripts; they have 'all' scope by default and are simpler for development.

evidence.note: Docs list Personal Access Tokens as a quickest way to start using the API and note they have the all scope.
evidence.label: sourced

nuances.text: Some partner or partner-documentation pages (Greenhouse integration docs) mention very short authorization code lifetimes and different endpoint paths; partner integrations may have additional constraints not documented in public Harvest docs.

evidence.note: Partner docs reference short code TTLs; this appears specific to partner integrations and is not explicitly described in Harvest public API docs, so verify with Harvest if you plan a deep partner integration.
evidence.label: unverified

nuances.text: Many developer tools expect OIDC discovery; because Harvest lacks .well-known discovery endpoints (probe), you may need to enter endpoints manually in OAuth tooling.

evidence.note: Docs provide explicit endpoints but probe shows no discovery metadata, so manual config is necessary for tools that cannot be configured with raw endpoints.
evidence.label: inferred

verdict.summary: Harvest exposes a self-serve OAuth2 flow you can register and use today; no app review is described in the docs. Expect a working dev app in under an hour and production availability immediately after you register and configure redirect URIs.

evidence.note: Docs show a self-serve Developers console and step-by-step OAuth flow; a community video demonstrates creating an app in the console.
evidence.label: sourced

timeToProd.assumes: You register a client in Harvest ID, implement the Authorization Code flow, and deploy your redirect endpoint (no external review needed).

evidence.note: Documentation describes creating OAuth2 Applications from the Developers section and shows the full code/token exchange; no review step is documented.
evidence.label: sourced

blockers.fix: Hardcode the documented endpoints from Harvest docs (authorize and token URLs) and implement flows using those URLs; fall back to manual configuration in tools that expect discovery.
blockers.cause: Harvest does not publish OpenID/OAuth discovery endpoints at common .well-known locations.
blockers.symptom: No OAuth discovery document (.well-known) available for Harvest

evidence.note: Live probe found no discovery metadata at common .well-known locations.
evidence.label: inferred

blockers.fix: Exchange the authorization code immediately server-side; if you encounter 'code expired' retry the authorization flow.
blockers.cause: Implementation delays or very short code lifetime (must exchange quickly).
blockers.symptom: Authorization code expired before exchange (errors during token exchange)

evidence.note: Harvest docs show the Authorization Code flow and token exchange; community partner docs (Greenhouse/partner) stress short code TTLs for some partner flows which may indicate some implementations have short lifetimes. Confirm code TTL with Harvest if you see very short expirations.
evidence.label: sourced

prerequisites.why: You must log in to Harvest ID to create an OAuth2 Application or Personal Access Token.
prerequisites.item: Harvest account (to access id.getharvest.com Developers section)

evidence.note: Docs point to the Developers section on Harvest ID for app creation.
evidence.label: sourced

prerequisites.why: OAuth Authorization Code flow requires a redirect URL registered with the client.
prerequisites.item: A callback/redirect URI hosted by your app

evidence.note: Redirect URL is required when registering an OAuth2 application.
evidence.label: sourced

prerequisites.why: Harvest uses Authorization Code flow and returns refresh tokens; code exchange must be done server-side.
prerequisites.item: Server to perform code exchange and securely store client_secret and refresh tokens

evidence.note: Token exchange examples show client_id and client_secret posted server-to-server; refresh token flow documented.
evidence.label: sourced
